summary_hint: who owes whom (maker to payee), the original principal, rate, payment amount and frequency, and the maturity date

typed_core.name: document_title
typed_core.why: identity — confirms this is a promissory/unsecured note

typed_core.name: note_date
typed_core.why: identity — the date the note was executed; anchors the obligation

typed_core.name: note_reference_number
typed_core.why: identity/dedup — distinguishes this note from others in the file

typed_core.name: maker_name
typed_core.why: identity — the obligor; is the borrower the maker (liability)? (flattened from person_or_entity[])

typed_core.name: maker_name_2
typed_core.why: identity — co-maker when present (flattened)

typed_core.name: maker_count
typed_core.why: disambiguator — how many makers the raw string resolved to

typed_core.name: payee_name
typed_core.why: identity — the lender/payee; is the borrower the payee (income)? (flattened from person_or_entity[])

typed_core.name: payee_name_2
typed_core.why: identity — co-payee when present (flattened)

typed_core.name: unsecured_indicator
typed_core.why: processor — confirms no collateral, changing how the debt/asset is treated (degraded from boolean)
typed_core.prompt_hint: "Unsecured" may be stated explicitly, implied by the absence of a security/collateral clause, or titled "Unsecured Promissory Note" — capture from any of these

typed_core.name: original_principal_amount
typed_core.why: processor — the face amount of the note

typed_core.name: current_principal_balance
typed_core.why: processor — the current amount owed/receivable (asset or liability value)

typed_core.name: interest_rate
typed_core.why: processor — the note rate (degraded from percent; may be stated "6.5%" or "six and one-half percent")

typed_core.name: payment_amount
typed_core.why: processor — the periodic payment (monthly debt or monthly income)

typed_core.name: payment_frequency
typed_core.why: disambiguator — monthly vs quarterly vs annual; without it payment_amount is unreadable (degraded from enum)

typed_core.name: first_payment_date
typed_core.why: processor — when payments begin

typed_core.name: payment_due_day_or_schedule
typed_core.why: processor — the due day / amortization schedule text

typed_core.name: maturity_date
typed_core.why: processor — when the note ends; income-continuance test (does it survive 3 years past closing)

typed_core.name: balloon_payment
typed_core.why: processor — a balloon changes the true payoff/continuance profile
typed_core.prompt_hint: Balloon terms often appear as "the entire unpaid balance shall be due on <date>" rather than a labeled balloon amount

typed_core.name: amortization_term
typed_core.why: processor — the amortization horizon (degraded from duration)

typed_core.name: prepayment_terms
typed_core.why: processor — penalty/prepay language affecting payoff

typed_core.name: default_and_acceleration_terms
typed_core.why: processor — default triggers a lender relies on when assessing the obligation

typed_core.name: note_city_and_state
typed_core.why: disambiguator — the place of execution; supports governing-law reading

typed_core.name: makers_signed
typed_core.why: processor — was the note executed by the maker(s) (degraded from signature[])

nested_lists.name: payment_history
nested_lists.shape_reason: payment history is the one genuinely repeating structure and can run to many rows on a seasoned note (a 4-year note = 48 monthly lines), so flat rows keep it under the 16,384 ceiling

fields.name: period
fields.why: the payment period the row covers

fields.name: remaining_balance
fields.why: balance remaining after the period's payment

rejected.name: issuer_name / issuer_address / issuer_phone / issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: a note is executed between maker and payee; "issuer" is captured by payee_name

rejected.name: party_names / party_addresses
rejected.reason: duplicate maker/payee names; addresses have no consumer here

rejected.name: property_address / loan_number / account_case_reference_number
rejected.reason: not present on an unsecured note (it is unsecured — no property)

rejected.name: governing_law
rejected.reason: narrative with no consumer; note_city_and_state carries the location signal

rejected.name: late_fee_and_grace_period
rejected.reason: object with no consumer; catch-all captures

rejected.name: remaining_payment_count_or_term
rejected.reason: TECHNICAL/derived — a computed conclusion, not a stated fact

rejected.name: income_expected_continuance_months
rejected.reason: TECHNICAL/derived — a judgment (continuance), which a rule makes from maturity_date; tags describe, rules judge

rejected.name: notary_or_witness / signature_blocks / notary_block
rejected.reason: execution captured by makers_signed; witness/notary rarely present and no consumer

encoding_variations: Principal stated both in numerals ("$50,000.00") and spelled out ("Fifty Thousand Dollars") — read the numeric figure but keep the snippet
Interest rate stated as a percent or in words; carry verbatim in the str value
Payment amount is ambiguous without frequency — a "$500" note could be $500/month or $500/quarter; payment_frequency is the required disambiguator
"Maker/Borrower/Obligor" and "Payee/Holder/Lender" are used interchangeably across templates — the model must map by role, not by the literal label

open_questions.recommendation: keep flat; revisit as a list only if a rule must address more than two makers/payees individually

open_questions.q: payment_history presence — many unsecured notes are provided at origination with no payment history yet.
options: treat empty as a missing-data flag
open_questions.recommendation: the list will legitimately be []; confirm that is acceptable rather than a missing-data flag

notes: No rules read this document today (rule floor is empty); fields are justified by identity, disambiguation, and processor use. An unsecured note is a promissory note with no collateral; its relevance is either a monthly debt the borrower pays or an income stream the borrower receives as payee.
Promissory-note vocabulary for the model: Maker/Obligor = who pays; Payee/Holder = who receives. Determining which side the mortgage borrower is on is the whole point.
